sources.title: Agentic AI harnesses
sources.issuer: Australian Signals Directorate / Australian Cyber Security Centre
sources.authorityNote: Government cyber-security guidance for government and large organisations; non-binding outside any separately applicable obligation.
sources.summary: Explains the agent harness as the software layer connecting an LLM to tools, data, memory and execution, and locates practical security and governance controls in that layer.
sources.applicability: Guidance for organisations adopting or considering agentic AI, especially executive decision-makers, CISOs and IT leaders. Inclusion does not determine legal applicability, implementation or control effectiveness.

provisions.title: Treat the harness as the governable control surface
provisions.summary: The harness supplies context, tools, permissions, execution, memory, connectors and observability, and should be assessed separately from the replaceable language model.
provisions.note: Original Atlas synopsis of the reviewed public sections; concept placement is Atlas interpretation.

provisions.title: Enforce permissions, approvals, monitoring and evidence in the harness
provisions.summary: Recommends least privilege, controlled tools and data, human approval for sensitive actions, output verification, protected logs, phased deployment and incident integration.
provisions.note: Guidance does not demonstrate that any organisation has implemented these practices or that they operate effectively.

proposedEdit.appendApplicability: Stable version 1.0 is distinguished from in-progress 1.01 research. Requirement references should identify their version; this review does not validate every requirement.

clarifications.limits: No new requirement mappings or changed requirement counts.

developments.title: Canada consultation exposes gaps in AI register disclosures
developments.summary: Respondents asked for consistent status labels, clearer AI decision roles, accountable contacts and links to recourse. These are reported views, not new obligations.
developments.implication: Review whether inventories explain how AI affects decisions and make missing information visible. The connection to Australian government guidance is Atlas interpretation; the Canadian report does not establish Australian obligations.
developments.question: Does our inventory show where AI changes decisions and who remains accountable?

questions.board: Does our inventory show where AI changes decisions and who remains accountable?
questions.executive: Which records lack verified status, ownership, update dates or recourse links?
questions.regulator: Can affected people understand the decision role and find a responsible contact?

canada-ai-register-feedback.askFor: Inventory records with decision roles, named owners, review dates, impact assessments and recourse contacts.
canada-ai-register-feedback.followUp: Which missing fields prevent a reviewer or affected person from understanding how a decision was made?

evidence.limitations: Government guidance, not binding law or proof of effective controls.
